burdens.description: Establish that belief in the Christian God is reasonable.
burdens.successCriteria: Provide a non-question-begging route from publicly assessable premises to the Christian God's existence or to justified belief in that existence.

burdens.description: Establish that truth, logic, knowledge, and reasoning require the Christian God.
burdens.successCriteria: Explain the dependence relation and show both that Christianity supplies the required foundation and that relevant alternatives cannot.

burdens.description: Defend divine revelation as a reliable epistemic route.
burdens.successCriteria: Explain how fallible people can identify genuine revelation, distinguish it from rivals, and receive truth without circularly assuming the source.

burdens.description: Show that non-Christian induction lacks adequate warrant while Christian revelation supplies it.
burdens.successCriteria: Identify the defect in probabilistic induction and demonstrate how revelation improves predictive warrant without merely asserting certainty.

burdens.description: State and defend an appropriate standard for reasonable belief.
burdens.successCriteria: Connect validity, evidential support, and proportionate confidence to belief while distinguishing reasonableness from absolute certainty.

burdens.description: Defend modest epistemic starting points against the charge of self-defeat.
burdens.successCriteria: Explain why using reason, senses, and shared experience is practically or epistemically warranted without claiming inaccessible ultimate certainty.

burdens.description: Test whether the pro case actually demonstrates its asserted foundation.
burdens.successCriteria: Identify missing inferential bridges, burden shifts, or circularity and directly request the demonstration needed to repair them.

burdens.description: Challenge the discriminatory power of claimed revelation.
burdens.successCriteria: Show how materially similar rival claims arise and require a publicly usable method that selects Christianity rather than merely restating it.

sections.title: Reasonable belief and the motion-level burden
sections.weightRationale: The debate formally asks whether belief is reasonable, so each side's governing criterion and initial burden posture shape every later exchange.

moves.speaker: Sye Ten Bruggencate
moves.sourceExcerpt: my argument premise one it's reasonable to believe that which is true premise two it's true that God exists conclusion therefore it's reasonable to believe that God exists now in order for an argument to be sound it must not only be valid in form but the premises must be true

passA.rationale: The form is explicit and stable, and it squarely states the pro motion route, but no warrant for the decisive existence premise appears in the selected act. Confidence substantially outruns that support. Charity is genuinely not tested by this constructive act, so the fixed 75 anchor is used.

passB.rationale: The formal route and its success condition are explicit, supporting constructive responsiveness and clarity. Its central premise substantially restates what the motion requires the pro side to establish, so evidence, calibration, and burden advancement remain weak. Charity is genuinely not tested by this self-contained opening and is fixed at 75.

adjudication.rationale: The syllogism is formally valid and exceptionally clear, but its first premise moves from a proposition's truth to the reasonableness of believing it without supplying the epistemic-access bridge, while its decisive God-exists premise is merely asserted. It states the central route but does not materially discharge the non-question-begging reasonableness criterion, so burden advancement remains below the competent band; charity is not tested and receives the fixed 75 anchor.

moves.speaker: Sye Ten Bruggencate
moves.sourceExcerpt: you can't know anything to be true unless you start with God everyone here knows that God exist why don't I present evidence when you come up to me and say you don't believe in God and I present you with evidence I'm saying that you're the judge you're not the judge God is the judge all of you know that he exists

passA.rationale: The locked reframe earns class-compliant coverage because it explains the alleged defect in the evidential demand and supplies an alternative epistemic priority. Numerically, that route is question-begging, unsupported, and materially weakens the con standard into a claim of ultimate listener authority. Its categorical universal-knowledge assertion is poorly calibrated.

passB.rationale: The locked reframe is structurally covered: it identifies a defect in public adjudication and supplies divine priority as the corrected route. Numerical quality is much lower because both universal God-knowledge and the authority reversal are asserted without a non-question-begging warrant, and the con standard is weakened into a claim of personal supremacy rather than public premise assessment.

adjudication.rationale: The move satisfies the locked reframe structurally by challenging listener adjudication and supplying divine priority, but it advances the adopted reasonableness and transcendental burdens only by asserting universal God-knowledge. Treating a request for publicly assessable premises as enthroning the listener weakens the con standard and shifts rather than completes the pro burden.

moves.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
moves.sourceExcerpt: what does it mean to say that something's reasonable in simplest terms it means we have good justification for accepting the proposition it means that we should be able to constru ruct an argument supporting the position that is both valid and sound and by sound I mean that our position is supported by evidence that the premises are true

passA.rationale: This is a coherent and precise governing standard that directly completes the con side's adopted standard-setting burden. Its warrants are conventional and explained, though the relationship among evidence, premise acceptance, and truth remains somewhat compressed. Charity is not tested, so it receives exactly 75.

passB.rationale: This supplies a clear and motion-level assessment standard with an intelligible connection among validity, premise support, and reasonable acceptance. The treatment of soundness as evidence-backed is compressed rather than fully defended, but the move strongly establishes the con side's governing burden. Charity is genuinely not tested and is fixed at 75.

moves.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
moves.sourceExcerpt: absolute certainty isn't a required component of knowledge because we have no good reason to think that absolute certainty in the ultimate sense is possible to attain we act in accordance with our beliefs ensuring that our beliefs are reasonable is the important issue which means that every time my opponent addresses knowledge or absolute certainty instead of belief and reasonableness he's actually waving a big red herring around

passA.rationale: Both halves of the locked reframe are explicit: the certainty demand is identified as misplaced and a proportionate action-guiding standard is offered. The move remains closely tied to the motion, marks its uncertainty, and represents the opponent's ultimate-reality demand fairly, with only a compressed defense of the fallibilist framework.

passB.rationale: The move explicitly explains why ultimate certainty is the wrong demand and answers the corrected question with a fallibilist, consequence-sensitive standard. The route is coherent, appropriately qualified, and central to both adopted con burdens, though the claim that certainty is completely irrelevant is slightly broader than its support.

sections.title: Ultimate reality, solipsism, and fallible access
sections.weightRationale: The brain-in-a-vat challenge dominates the opening and cross-examination and tests whether modest fallibilism is self-defeating.

moves.speaker: Sye Ten Bruggencate
moves.sourceExcerpt: you need to be able to know what's ultimately real to know what's true I submit that you can't know what's ultimately real without Revelation from God how do I know what's real the same way all of you do Revelation from the god that all of you know exists Christians profess that truth profess atheists suppress it

passA.rationale: This is central constructive material and states its intended bridge clearly enough, but neither the necessity of ultimate access nor the reliability of revelation is demonstrated. The suppression claim adds an unsupported representation of dissenters' epistemic state, and the categorical confidence is radically disproportionate to the warrant in the selected span.

passB.rationale: The move advances a central constructive route, but it leaves each indispensable dependence relation unsupported: why ordinary truth requires ultimate access, why revelation supplies that access, and why the revelation is specifically reliable. The unqualified suppression attribution also overstates both warrant and the live alternative, lowering calibration and charity.

adjudication.rationale: The passage directly states the pro side's ultimate-reality and revelation route, making it a necessary central sub-burden rather than peripheral material. It nevertheless supplies no dependence argument from ordinary truth to ultimate access, no reliability mechanism for revelation, and no warrant for attributing suppression to dissenters, so it does not complete either adopted burden.

moves.speaker: Sye Ten Bruggencate
moves.sourceExcerpt: you've admitted you could be a brain in a f I haven't admitted that I can be I haveed that I cannot prove that I'm not could that's right so therefore it follows that you could be the fact that something hasn't been proved to false does not mean that it's possible or true on what basis do you trust your senses and reasoning on their continued reliability at producing effective results

passA.rationale: The basis question has topical contact, but the principal inference attacks a concession the con side did not make. Failure to disprove does not itself establish possibility, so the route is invalid at its core. The move is confident despite the explicit correction and materially weakens the live fallibilist position, keeping responsiveness inside the locked substitution range.

passB.rationale: The modal inference does not follow from non-disproof, and the selected exchange immediately records the distinction. Because the act attacks a stronger concession than D05-M006 made, responsiveness stays within the lower weaker-substitution band; the trailing request for a basis is relevant but does not repair the inference or the misrepresentation.

adjudication.rationale: The audio-verified exchange immediately distinguishes inability to disprove a vat scenario from establishing its possibility, leaving the pro modal inference without warrant. The trailing request for a basis has real topical contact, but it does not support the principal inference or repair the substitution of a stronger concession than the con side made.

moves.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
moves.sourceExcerpt: you can't prove that your the reality you experience is actually real in an ultimate sense it's been expressed in many ways one of the more common is that you're a brain in a vat the general consensus among philosophers seems to be that there's no current solution to this problem but I'll concede that there appears to be no ultimate absolute solution but I'm stuck dealing with the reality I experience

passA.rationale: The concession accurately accepts the strongest skeptical pressure and then answers the corrected fallibilist question without pretending to solve hard solipsism. The practical bridge is coherent and well calibrated, though its appeal to a general philosophical consensus is not documented and the epistemic warrant beyond unavoidable practice remains compressed.

passB.rationale: The move fairly grants the force of the skeptical target and gives a coherent fallibilist reason to continue inquiry under a corrected standard. The appeal to a general philosophical consensus and practical unavoidability does not fully establish an epistemic warrant, so evidence and burden completion remain below the strongest band.

moves.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
moves.sourceExcerpt: if something hasn't been demonstrated to be impossible is it then possible no and if something hasn't been demonstrated to be false then that is it then true no great so then why is it that when we talk about this and I honestly recognize that I can't demonstrate that I'm not a brain and aat you keep coming back with I can't know that I'm not a brain and aat or that I could be a brain and aat neither of which have I said or conceited

passA.rationale: The parallel diagnostic is explicit, logically decisive, and directly defeats the targeted modal inference if accepted. It relies on concessions obtained within the exchange, precisely preserves the con side's narrower anti-proof position, and avoids overstating what the diagnosis establishes. Only the compressed oral phrasing leaves minor room for improvement.

passB.rationale: The parallel tests isolate the exact modal and epistemic error and then apply it to the recurring brain-in-a-vat claim. The diagnosis is explicit, fairly represents the preceding inference, and would defeat that inference if accepted; its warrant is supplied by the opponent's direct answers within the selected dialogue.

sections.title: Logical absolutes and worldview accounting
sections.weightRationale: Whether logic needs and receives a specifically Christian foundation is the core transcendental claim and carries the largest single section weight.

moves.speaker: Sye Ten Bruggencate
moves.sourceExcerpt: if biochemical reactions are all that you are thinking then all that you can say is that what you perceive to be logical true and Absolut necessary is nothing more than the result of chemical reactions in your brain if Matt's worldview is true then our thoughts our brains are just evolved meat machines and our thoughts are the byproduct of the chemical reactions in our evolved Brains you can't get truth from that

passA.rationale: The conditional caricature is vivid and recoverable, but the opponent explicitly distinguished methodological from philosophical naturalism and did not adopt reductive biochemical exhaustiveness. No bridge shows why a physical process cannot token truth or valid inference. The result is poorly warranted, overconfident, and only loosely relevant to the actual adopted con burden.

passB.rationale: The move is topical to the transcendental burden, but the locked class reflects that the opponent did not adopt the reductive position being attacked. Even on its own terms, the passage supplies no bridge from physical realization to the impossibility of truth-tracking thought, so the central inference, evidence, and representation are seriously underdeveloped.

adjudication.rationale: The conditional biochemical-fizz argument is recoverable and its intended conclusion is clear despite derisive metaphors, supporting the lower edge of the competent clarity band. Its numerical weakness belongs principally to the missing bridge from physical realization to inability to token truth and to its materially weaker reconstruction of the con position, rather than to unrecoverable expression.

moves.speaker: Sye Ten Bruggencate
moves.sourceExcerpt: you are asserting that no one but you can account no one can account for logical absolutes except for within your worldview and I'm asking you to demonstrate that that's true well I have no problem doing that logical absolutes reflect the thinking of God what they reflect the thinking of God by his Revelation the same way you do see because we all appeal to logical absolutes

passA.rationale: The move contacts one indispensable component by naming a proposed Christian ground, so responsiveness remains within the locked partial range. Naming reflection and revelation is compatibility rather than an explanatory warrant, and the separate alternative-account demand is untouched. Its certainty is unsupported. Charity is not genuinely tested by this bare attempted account, so it is fixed at 75.

passB.rationale: The act reaches one indispensable target component and therefore remains within the locked partial-answer range. Identifying logical absolutes with divine thought states compatibility rather than demonstrating a dependence relation, while revelation is invoked without an independent warrant; the comparative component is left unanswered. Charity is genuinely not tested and is fixed at 75.

adjudication.rationale: Identifying logical absolutes with God's thought and invoking revelation contacts a central component of the transcendental and revelation burdens, but naming the proposed ground is not an explanation of dependence. The answer leaves both the requested demonstration and the exclusion of alternatives unresolved, so its burden contribution is relevant but weak; charity is not tested and receives 75.

moves.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
moves.sourceExcerpt: if we agree that we must first presuppose the laws of logic then we shouldn't expand this potential Problem by presupposing something beyond the laws of logic we agree they're true when Sai claims that God serves as a foundation Beyond The Logical absolutes he's violating aam's Razer and when he claims that no other worldview can account for The Logical absolutes he needs to demonstrate the truth of this claim how did he do this has he done it

passA.rationale: The move explicitly diagnoses the expansion beyond shared logic and answers with a minimal common starting point, satisfying the locked reframe strongly. Its burden placement and target representation are fair. The parsimony warrant and claim that the further why-question may be incoherent are plausible but compressed rather than fully defended.

passB.rationale: The move explains why the metaphysical demand may add an unnecessary posit and answers the corrected demand with mutually accepted logical starting points. It directly advances both con foundations and critique burdens, though the parsimony warrant and the claim that stopping at logic is preferable remain philosophically compressed.

moves.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
moves.sourceExcerpt: not only has he not demonstrated that his worldview can account for the absolutes he's merely asserted that his God has the necessary qualities to do so which is a vacuous claim he also hasn't demonstrated that it's even possible to account for the absolutes when He suggests that we must borrow from his worldview he actually hasn't demonstrated any worldview that is more than a simple assertion that his worldview solved a problem where is the demonstration of the truth of this

passA.rationale: Those two omissions are indispensable to the selected pro transcendental conclusion, so the diagnosis directly defeats it unless repaired. The analysis is precise, burden-proportionate, and accurately distinguishes a named solution from an explained dependence. Evidence consists chiefly of the opponent's visible assertions, leaving only a bounded documentation gap.

passB.rationale: These are the two indispensable bridges in the selected transcendental case, and their absence would defeat its conclusion without requiring a rival metaphysics. The diagnosis is precise and tightly tied to the opponent's stated assertions; some broad claims about explanatory power are stronger than the selected evidence alone, preventing exceptional calibration.

sections.title: Reason, circularity, and induction
sections.weightRationale: These exchanges test whether ordinary epistemic practice is viciously circular and whether probabilistic induction needs revealed certainty.

moves.speaker: Sye Ten Bruggencate
moves.sourceExcerpt: how does Matt know whether they've been reliable in the past how does Matt know they're reliable now how does Matt know that they're going to be reliable do you know why because he uses them to prove it it's a vicious circle is it circular to use your reasoning to justify your reasoning it's a practical necessity is it circular I'm using reason because it continues to produce effective results do you use your reasoning in determining that yes well then you're using your reasoning to prove your reasoning

passA.rationale: The alleged circle and its consequence are explicit enough to satisfy the locked diagnostic class. The move materially pressures an ultimate self-validation claim and fairly tracks the immediate answer. Its weakness is treating all epistemic circularity as vicious without distinguishing unavoidable rule-circularity or the con side's modest practical warrant, so the diagnosis is useful but not complete.

passB.rationale: If the track-record defense purports to establish reason's validity, the identified dependence is a serious circularity diagnosis and directly pressures the con foundations burden. The move does not distinguish unavoidable rule-circularity from a premise-circular proof or show why the former is vicious, so coherence, warrant, and calibration remain materially below the top diagnostic band.

moves.speaker: Sye Ten Bruggencate
moves.sourceExcerpt: so if I said to you you just proen I'm never going to die because I've never died in the past would that not be a logical fallacy that's true for everybody right up until the point they have so therefore that being the case on what basis do you assume that the future will be like the past I assume that in the future you will die that's not my question

passA.rationale: The counterexamples are intelligible and would defeat the stronger certainty claim, which gives the move some evidential and inferential value. They do not engage the actual qualified target, so relevance and responsiveness are limited and class-bounded. Treating a probabilistic claim as deductive entailment materially weakens the opponent and overstates what the examples accomplish.

passB.rationale: The examples do show that observed regularity does not deductively entail the next result, but that is materially stronger than the probabilistic target. Accordingly responsiveness remains in the lower weaker-substitution band, and the mismatch also limits burden advancement and charity even though the counterexamples themselves are understandable and relevant to a broader induction dispute.

adjudication.rationale: The mortality and house-color examples clearly show that past cases do not deductively entail the next case, giving recognizable contact with the induction dispute. D05-M014 had expressly limited its claim to probabilistic broad similarity, however, so the response attacks a materially stronger reconstruction and belongs in the 35–49 weaker-substitution band rather than the substantial-issue-change band.

moves.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
moves.sourceExcerpt: we live our lives by inference and induction we are under the general assumption that the future is going to be pretty much like the past not exactly like the past and that is because we have this trend of that always happening I'm not asserting that there is absolutely no difference in the future I'm saying that I believe and I believe that I am rationally justified in believing that the future is going to be pretty much like the past

passA.rationale: Coverage of the locked immediate target is complete and unusually well calibrated: the source of the expectation and its fallible scope are both stated. The empirical trend is relevant support, though the induction warrant remains necessarily compressed and the move does not solve the separate circularity problem, which the response lock correctly excludes from its target.

passB.rationale: Every indispensable part of the immediate request is covered, supporting the locked full-answer score, and the modality is carefully limited. Past regularity is relevant inductive support but does not non-circularly justify the general reliability of induction, leaving a material warrant gap. No live alternative is represented or attacked, so charity is genuinely not tested and fixed at 75.

adjudication.rationale: The answer coherently limits induction to a broad, fallible expectation based on observed regularity and therefore avoids the deductive entailment the next challenge attributes to it. Its route remains materially compressed because past regularity does not itself provide a non-circular ultimate vindication of induction, but that residual gap does not erase the coherent probabilistic answer; charity is untested and fixed at 75.

moves.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
moves.sourceExcerpt: what would you predict the next house is going to be that's the world we live in a world where we are making predictions based on probabilities from our experience of the past we are not declaring that we have tuned into the absolute reality and have divine revelation that the next house is going to be read and that we can't be wrong about that it is called inference and induction we are not making claims that we are certain or that it couldn't be different

passA.rationale: Both parts of the reframe are explicit, and the response precisely preserves the limited inferential strength of induction. It directly advances the con foundations burden, fairly identifies the opponent's stronger reconstruction, and calibrates confidence to probability. The warrant from past experience is compressed but appropriately modest rather than circularly presented as a proof.

passB.rationale: The act accurately identifies that the challenge tests a certainty claim induction does not make and then supplies the corrected probabilistic answer. It is explicit, fair, and well calibrated; the remaining limitation is that experience-based success is asserted as practical warrant without a full account of induction's deeper circularity.

sections.title: Revelation, scripture, and rival religious claims
sections.weightRationale: Because revelation is offered as the epistemic solution, its accessibility, corrigibility, and discriminatory power are load-bearing.

moves.speaker: Sye Ten Bruggencate
moves.sourceExcerpt: I don't do Bible studies with with non-believers Jesus would not put his word up to the authority of you to judge whether it's true or not I will Proclaim I will Proclaim I will proclaim the truth of scripture to you but I will not discuss the truth of it with you not when an atheist says well it's false because of this because I don't believe with their presuppositions I will not put the word of God up to the the test of the aist

passA.rationale: The refusal is verbally clear but does not supply the requested reconciliation or a public warrant for revelation. It is circular relative to the adopted revelation and reasonableness burdens, shifts the issue from the alleged error to the questioner's status, and represents the challenge as hostile adjudication rather than a request for explanation. Responsiveness therefore stays low within the locked substitution band.

passB.rationale: The response clearly states its procedural stance but changes the issue from reconciling an apparent scriptural error to whether an outsider may judge scripture. Proclamation supplies neither the requested reconciliation nor a public reliability warrant, and the categorical refusal conflicts with the adopted burden to explain how fallible recipients identify genuine revelation.

adjudication.rationale: The categorical refusal and proclamation are far more confident than the supplied reliability warrant. The speaker also recasts a request to reconcile an apparent scriptural error as an atheist declaration that scripture is false, even though the immediate exchange explicitly distinguishes the request for explanation, making the representation materially weaker rather than wholly unrecognizable.

moves.speaker: Sye Ten Bruggencate
moves.sourceExcerpt: I'll ask the Muslim why do you not believe the the Bible today and you know what the Muslim will say because it's been corrupted and then I'll ask the Muslim what does your Quran say about whether the words of Allah can be corrupted and I'll say it cannot see that's the problem if the Quran is true the Bible is true and because the Bible is true the Quran is false

passA.rationale: If its scriptural premises and interpretation hold, the contradiction supplies a recognizable discriminator against one rival, so it advances one indispensable component of the locked target. Those premises are asserted without textual support and compress a complex rival position. The broader intra-Christian and generic cross-tradition selection problem remains unanswered, requiring partial-range responsiveness.

passB.rationale: This is a concrete discriminator and reaches one indispensable part of the rival-revelation target, keeping responsiveness within the partial-answer band. The textual premises and the bridge from an Islamic inconsistency to the Bible's truth are asserted rather than established in the span, while generic rival and intra-Christian selection problems remain unresolved.

moves.speaker: Sye Ten Bruggencate
moves.sourceExcerpt: that defense is available and I'll be happy to discuss anybody who claims that Zeus is their God or who who claims that the Flying Spaghetti Monster as you have on your shirts out if they want to claim that I'll be happy to debate them I'm saying that no other gods exist because that's what the Bible says all the gods of the nations are Idols but the Lord made the heavens

passA.rationale: The explicit concession answers one part of the parity question and is clearly stated, justifying partial-range responsiveness. The biblical assertion does not provide the requested common selection method and instead presupposes the contested revelation. Confidence in exclusivity therefore far exceeds the supplied warrant. The reply recognizes the rival structure but lightly trivializes it through the Flying Spaghetti Monster example.

passB.rationale: The first component is directly and fairly answered through concession, which supports the locked partial-answer score. The second indispensable component—a common discriminator—receives only a citation to the very revelation under challenge, so the reply is circular as a comparative warrant and does not materially complete the revelation or transcendental burdens.

adjudication.rationale: The reply fairly recognizes and concedes that rival traditions can use the same defense, which answers one target component and avoids a gross caricature despite the dismissive Flying Spaghetti Monster comparison. Its only discriminator is the Bible's own denial of rival gods, so confidence in Christian exclusivity remains disproportionate and the central revelation burden is shifted back to future debates rather than advanced by a public selecting method.

moves.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
moves.sourceExcerpt: they can't all be right but they can all be wrong David hum famous famously told us that Revelation is necessarily first person and to everyone else it's here say while many Christians claim divine revelation some even claiming that the truth has been revealed to them in such a way that there's no possibility that they could be wrong there's hardly any points of Doctrine upon which all these purported conduits of divine revelation agree which means that some if not all of them are wrong

passA.rationale: The diagnosis directly attacks revelation's claimed reliability: incompatible conduits cannot all be right, and the selected pro mechanism offers no method for selecting among them. The conceptual inference is strong, fair, and burden-central. Specific denominational breadth and the attributed Humean point are not documented in the span, creating a bounded evidence gap rather than undermining the core parity problem.

passB.rationale: Conflicting purported revelations directly undermine bare revelation as a shared reliable route unless a selecting method is supplied, so the diagnosis reaches a decisive premise of the pro burden. The general empirical claims are plausible but only broadly supported within the span, and the characterization of revelation as hearsay compresses possible public corroboration.

moves.speaker: Unidentified audience member
moves.sourceExcerpt: for any given religious tradition and when I'm not just talking about Islam I'm talking about you know Zeus Thor any given particular religious tradition why can't they just fill in those boxes with their given ex's I.E I believe the truth exists I believe a necessary presupposition for that truth existing is that Thor exists Ergo Thor exists why isn't that defense available to anyone from any Rel religious tradition

passA.rationale: The parity test exposes a decisive missing bridge: the general form does not itself select Christianity. It is logically clear, directly responsive to both the asserted Christian account and the narrow Islam reply, and fairly states the target before criticism. As a conceptual countermodel it needs little empirical evidence, though it does not independently prove that every rival has equal total support.

passB.rationale: The parity test precisely exposes that a necessity-and-revelation template does not select Christianity merely by inserting its preferred deity. If no asymmetric discriminator is supplied, the exclusivity burden fails without a complete rival worldview. The hypothetical is structurally probative, although it does not by itself establish that every rival has equal independent warrant.

sections.title: Corrigibility, burden placement, and closing synthesis
sections.weightRationale: The final exchanges clarify whether the pro position admits correction and whether its comparative claims were demonstrated across the full debate.

moves.speaker: Sye Ten Bruggencate
moves.sourceExcerpt: that's a great question and it's a it's a huge misunderstanding of the argument I'm not saying logical absolutes or absolutes of any kind therefore God I'm saying You must start with the god of Christianity the only God exists that exists in order to make sense of any absolutes it's not absolutes therefore God it's God therefore absolutes

passA.rationale: The immediate misunderstanding is expressly identified and the intended direction is stated with excellent precision, strongly satisfying the locked reframe. That clarification does not demonstrate the presupposition's truth, explanatory dependence, or Christian exclusivity, so coherence, evidence, relevance, and calibration remain materially limited even while representation of the immediate question is fair.

passB.rationale: Both steps of the locked reframe are explicit and unusually clear, justifying high structural responsiveness. The correction is interpretive rather than evidential: it restates Christianity as a starting presupposition but supplies no warrant for necessity, exclusivity, or the dependence relation, so coherence, evidence, and burden completion remain mixed.

adjudication.rationale: The move very clearly corrects the inferential direction from absolutes-to-God to God-as-starting-presupposition and therefore strongly satisfies the locked reframe. That interpretive clarification is central but supplies no demonstration of the presupposition's truth, necessity, dependence relation, or Christian exclusivity, leaving its burden advancement topical and materially incomplete.

moves.speaker: Sye Ten Bruggencate

passB.rationale: The act is recognizable as a synthesis of the pro case and therefore receives constructive responsiveness, but its decisive dilemma and universal-knowledge premise remain unsupported. Attributing rejection to love of sin caricatures the live con position and radically exceeds the supplied warrant, while the exhortation does not repair the adopted reasonableness or transcendental burdens.

adjudication.rationale: The closing is recognizably connected to the pro motion-level case, but it restates the unsupported Christianity-or-absurdity dilemma rather than completing the reasonableness or transcendental success criteria. Universal God-knowledge, sinful motivation, and threatened consequences do not supply the missing bridge, while the attribution that dissenters knowingly choose absurdity from love of sin is both radically overconfident and grossly uncharitable.
